messages.author: 67b2fdd14618dbab
messages.subject: calculateDiffMeth -> wmean vs mean
parts:
Hi, 
I hope that I don't repeat I common question here... but there is my little problem.

if I use a minimum coverage that I consider enough to estimate the percentage of methylation of my individuals, should I used mean instead of wmean when I perform the function calculateDiffMeth.
In other words, if my minimum coverage filter is enough to estimate the methylation of an individuals, why giving more weight to individuals because they have more coverage ?
I think about that because when I compare both setting with my dataset, I see cases where wmean consider the CpG with more then 20% of difference but mean have less than 5% of difference. 

If wmean is a necessity, do you thing that using an intersect of both wmean and mean result could be a solution to ensure that a difference higher than 20% is present under both setting ?

thank you for your help.

Martin

messages.author: ac5ddd29540c757f
messages.subject: Re: calculateDiffMeth -> wmean vs mean
parts:
I  also have been wondering about this and whether there is any guideline out there on this topic.
I found this article that mentions it briefly 
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3523709/
"'Leveling’ the playing field for analyses of single-base resolution DNA methylomes"

from the paper above: " For example, imagine two sites in a region, one with 90 methylated reads from 100 total reads and another with one methylated read out of two total reads. The methylation level for this region will be very different depending on whether more weight is given to the first site or if equal weight is given to both sites"

messages.author: 67b2fdd14618dbab
messages.subject: Re: calculateDiffMeth -> wmean vs mean
parts:
Thank for you answer Linda.

I think it is true that the estimate of methylation level will be affected when you coverage is low. But if you have a descent minimum coverage (like 10X or more) and you want to compare group of individuals CpG by CpG, I think that if you estimate with enough coverage (meaning enough precision) you should not give more weight on an individual that have better sequencing success for the loci of this CpG. Giving more weight to an individual inside a group will affect group mean and if this individual is different from the rest of the group for an unknow biological reason, all the group will sudenly be more similar to this individual but they are not suppose to be. But maybe I miss something too.

Martin

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Re: calculateDiffMeth -> wmean vs mean
parts: I would go with weighted mean 1) logistic regression already gives higher weight to samples that are highly covered, this is just how it works, we don't change the default behaviour 2) imagine you have a region that is 50% methylated and covered 100X, if for some reason same region has less coverage in one sample such as 10X, you can simulate the situation by downsampling 100X region to 10X, if you do that you would get 20% or 80% methylated regions not infrequently.  So the moment you drop the coverage to 10X, you become less confident that your 10X covered CpG has the correct methylation level compared to same CpG covered 100X.
